estimator_specs.name: Exact finite-sample and Gumbel CDF for centered exponential maximum

assumptions: Each X_i follows the rate-one exponential distribution with CDF F(x) = 1 - exp(-x) for x >= 0
The exponential support is [0, infinity), so M_n >= 0 and Y_n >= -log(n)
The centering is by log(n), not by n, sqrt(n), or other scales
Convergence is pointwise for each fixed y in R, not uniform
problem_card.asymptotic_regime: Fixed-y pointwise convergence as n -> infinity: for every fixed y in R, P(Y_n <= y) converges to exp(-exp(-y))
problem_card.desired_theorem_type: Exact finite-sample CDF with support-aware branch, pointwise weak convergence to Gumbel distribution
problem_card.dgp: X_1, X_2, ..., X_n are independent and identically distributed rate-one exponential random variables with CDF F(x) = 1 - exp(-x) for x >= 0 and support [0, infinity).
problem_card.estimand: The exact finite-sample CDF of the centered sample maximum Y_n = M_n - log(n), where M_n = max(X_1, ..., X_n), evaluated at the observed centered maximum value. The asymptotic target is the standard Gumbel CDF G(y) = exp(-exp(-y)).
nuisance_quantities: The sample size n (known from the data)
problem_card.observed_data: One sample of n independent rate-one exponential observations, where n >= 2.

theory_semantic_material.proof_evidence_boundary: LLM derivations, retrieval hits, and simulation predictions are proposal or diagnostic evidence only. Formal proof evidence requires AXLE/local Lean kernel verification of the intended formal claim.

question.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Fisher and Tippett (1928) and Gnedenko (1943). Let X_1,...,X_n be independent rate-one exponential random variables, let M_n=max_i X_i, and let Y_n=M_n-log n. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the exact finite-n CDF of M_n and the support-aware finite-n CDF of Y_n, including the branch below -log n. Then prove pointwise for every real y that P(Y_n <= y) converges to the standard Gumbel CDF exp(-exp(-y)). Make independence, the exponential support, the normalization log n, the fixed-y limiting argument, and the distinction between an exact finite-n law and its asymptotic approximation auditable. Do not replace the maximum by the minimum, omit the finite-n support branch, center by n or log(n-1), reverse a CDF or survival function, claim finite-n equality with the Gumbel law, or generalize the result to arbitrary parent distributions without domain-of-attraction conditions. The required model-authored Python artifact is est_exponential_maximum_gumbel and must implement run_estimator(request) exactly for the frozen closed sample contract. It returns the sample size, maximum, centered maximum, exact finite-n CDF evaluated at that centered value, and standard Gumbel CDF evaluated at that value. Exploratory Python or R may check identities. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment generates independent rate-one exponential samples at several predeclared sample sizes, invokes the exact accepted estimator, verifies the exact finite-n CDF empirically with Monte Carlo uncertainty, and assesses the Gumbel approximation over a preregistered finite grid as n grows. This assessment is distributional implementation evidence, not proof, a universal extreme-value theorem, finite-n Gumbel equality, source replication, novelty, tail extrapolation beyond the frozen grid, or formal proof. Lean formalization is not applicable.
question.title: Gumbel limit for the maximum of exponential observations

simulation_ademp_spec.aim: Verify that the exact finite-sample CDF formula is correctly implemented and assess the Gumbel approximation error across increasing sample sizes on a preregistered finite evaluation grid.
dgps: Rate-one exponential distribution: X_i ~ Exp(rate=1) with CDF F(x) = 1 - exp(-x) for x >= 0
expected_theoretical_behavior: For each fixed sample size n and evaluation point y >= -log(n), the empirical CDF should be close to the exact finite-n CDF (1 - exp(-y)/n)^n within Monte Carlo uncertainty
The exact finite-n CDF should differ from the Gumbel CDF exp(-exp(-y)) by approximately O(1/n) for moderate n
As n increases, the exact finite-n CDF should approach the Gumbel CDF pointwise
methods: For each frozen sample size n in {10, 50, 100, 250, 500}, generate M independent samples of size n from the rate-one exponential distribution
For each sample, compute the sample maximum M_n and centered maximum Y_n = M_n - log(n)
Invoke the estimator est_exponential_maximum_gumbel with the sample to obtain exact_cdf_at_centered and gumbel_cdf_at_centered
Compute the empirical CDF of the M centered maxima and compare to the exact finite-n CDF using the preregistered Monte Carlo uncertainty rule
Retain exact finite-n CDF, Gumbel CDF, and approximation error for each sample size and evaluation point
performance_measures: Empirical CDF of centered maxima vs. exact finite-n CDF: mean absolute error and maximum absolute error over the M replicates
Exact finite-n CDF vs. Gumbel CDF: pointwise error at each evaluation point
Approximation error trend: how the error decreases as n increases
stress_tests: Boundary case: y close to -log(n) (near the support boundary)
Extreme case: y far above -log(n) (deep in the support)
Small sample: n = 10 (finite-n effects are large)
Large sample: n = 500 (Gumbel approximation should be accurate)
